source.title: Breathing above the brain stem: volitional control and attentional modulation in humans

confidence_rationale: Direct human intracranial evidence that breathing entrains widespread cortical/limbic activity (gamma envelope tracks breath) AND that VOLITIONALLY paced breathing changes that entrainment, raising iEEG-breath coherence in a frontotemporal-insular network. This establishes the structural premise of MECH-109 -- a voluntary top-down route by which the agent alters how strongly the breath rhythm organises cortical activity. It does not measure planning or plan abandonment, and small epilepsy-patient samples raise transfer risk.
failure_signatures: No planning, deliberation or plan-abandonment measure was taken, so increased breath-cortex coherence under volitional pacing is not shown to change any planning computation.

Volitional pacing and attention to breath engaged overlapping but distinct networks, so the 'voluntary handle' may be partly an attentional/interoceptive effect rather than a control-plane clock intervention.
Data come from a small number of epilepsy patients with clinically placed electrodes, limiting generalisation.

mapping.source_claim_statement: iEEG activity tracks the breathing cycle across widespread cortical and limbic structures; volitionally paced breathing increases iEEG-breath coherence in a frontotemporal-insular network, while attention to breathing increases coherence in anterior cingulate, premotor, insular and hippocampal cortices.
mapping.ree_translation: Voluntary breath control is not only a brainstem motor act; it changes how tightly cortex (including hippocampus, the MECH-108 sweep substrate) is locked to the respiratory rhythm. That is the necessary structural condition for breath to be a top-down handle on a breath-locked planning clock.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Coherence change is not a demonstrated change in plan-sweep rate or abandonment; attention and volition are partly confounded; the 'only handle' exclusivity is untested.
mapping.source_context: Adult epilepsy patients with intracranial electrodes; conditions of spontaneous breathing, volitionally paced breathing and attention to breath (tasks adapted from CBT and meditation practice).

confidence_components.notes: Rare human iEEG with a volitional-breathing manipulation, which is the manipulation MECH-109 names. Sample size and clinical population limit source quality; the downstream planning DV is missing.
